shouldFix.title: subjectDigestIdentity compares digest declarations but never measures the named subject file
evidence: subjectDigestIdentity requires predecessorVerdictFindings[N].subjectSha256 to equal the subject entry in recordedInputs and requires each review's start/end/expected declarations to equal that value. None of its operands is sha256 of the bytes at docs/coop/artifacts/host-effect-authorization.vN.json, and it does not require that path to exist.

The adjacent provenanceCheck supplies exactly the missing operation for review files: it requires the review path to exist and sha256(file bytes) to equal both the lane digest and recordedInputs before extraction. No analogous subject-file existence or byte-hash check appears in laneCheck, subjectDigestIdentity, or another registerCoverageRule member.

A concrete in-memory countermodel starts with the canonical v23 subject and changes only its top-level date to 2099-01-01. Those changed subject bytes hash to c569f169236f4a638e8af7d8eb02fc4f9ab22c01c5555e1eddc8fdb03a460b5d, while predecessorVerdictFindings.v23.subjectSha256, recordedInputs, and both pinned reviews' subjectSha256Expected/AtStart/AtEnd remain de5c9d8045bcae73fb9c79eb020ea5e38890d4573a23e951ef74f4e3f17b109c. Every comparison stated by subjectDigestIdentity still passes because the actual subject hash is never computed. Removing the subject path produces the same result under the named check.

The generic remeasurementClause says a moved cited source is remeasured, but the governing mechanical laneCheck neither invokes such a subject measurement nor specifies that a missing or hash-mismatched subject refuses. It cannot make subjectDigestIdentity detect movement without first adding the omitted path-existence and byte-hash operands.

The live corpus is clean: every v6-v23 subject path exists and its actual Python hashlib digest equals its recordedInputs entry and register subjectSha256. That makes the rule gap a SHOULD-FIX rather than a blocker.
shouldFix.impact: A historical subject can be replaced or removed after both reviews freeze while every review-file provenance check, register completeness check, and subjectDigestIdentity declaration comparison continues to pass. A successor can then attribute frozen verdicts to bytes that no longer match the registered subject custody pin.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Before comparing digest declarations, require the canonical subject path docs/coop/artifacts/host-effect-authorization.vN.json to exist and compute sha256 of its bytes. Require that measured digest to equal recordedInputs[path] and predecessorVerdictFindings[N].subjectSha256; missing path or mismatch MUST refuse. Then retain the existing review start/end/expected equality checks.
